newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Dlr pushes Moroccan dirham to near 20 yr low.
newsitem.headline: Dlr pushes Moroccan dirham to near 20 yr low.

text.p: Morocco's dirham on Monday fell to its lowest level in nearly two decades against the soaring U.S. currency, reaching 10 dirhams against one dollar, a Moroccan official said.

"The dirham (falling) value on Monday against the soaring U.S. dollar should not be considered as a slip but simply as a result of weighting in the basket of hard currencies," the official who declined to be named told Reuters.
Exchange rates against the Moroccan dirham are fixed by the central bank through a mechanism of "basket of hard currencies" which is not disclosed to the public, the official added.
The U.S. dollar remains the main currency for Morocco's multi-billion commodity and energy imports, a Casablanca-based stockbroker said.
The average rate for the U.S. dollar varied between 8.1424 and 9.3903 during the last two decades, he added.
